trials.name: Clarity AD
trials.population: Participants with early Alzheimer's disease/mild cognitive impairment
trials.primary_endpoint: Change from Baseline in the Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) at 18 Months
trials.results_summary: Lecanemab significantly reduced amyloid burden and resulted in a 27% slower clinical decline on the CDR-SB over 18 months compared to placebo, validating the therapeutic relevance of amyloid removal in early AD.

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2
trials.population: Participants with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease and specific PET scan criteria
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline on the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS)
trials.results_summary: Donanemab significantly slowed cognitive and functional decline (by 35% on iADRS) in early symptomatic AD patients. The trial successfully utilized tau PET staging, demonstrating the practical utility of the biological staging proposed in the criteria.

trials.name: IDEAS
trials.population: Medicare beneficiaries with MCI or dementia of uncertain etiology
trials.primary_endpoint: ≥ 30% change between intended and actual patient management within 90 days
trials.results_summary: Amyloid PET imaging significantly altered patient management in over 60% of cases, demonstrating the clinical utility of Core 1 biomarkers in diagnostically uncertain populations.

trials.name: ADNI3
trials.population: Cognitively normal, MCI, and mild AD dementia participants
trials.primary_endpoint: Rate of change in cognition and biomarker correlations over 5 years
trials.results_summary: Validated the temporal sequencing of Alzheimer's biomarkers and supported the accuracy of biofluid markers against PET and autopsy gold standards, forming the foundational evidence base for staging.

Diagnostic Accuracy of a Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217 Immunoassay for Alzheimer Disease Pathology

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence heavily supports the biological framework proposed by the workgroup, though real-world application currently faces regulatory and infrastructural hurdles. Large Phase 3 trials (Clarity AD and TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2) definitively demonstrated that identifying and removing Core 1/2 biomarkers (amyloid and tau) yields clinical benefit, fundamentally shifting the paradigm toward biomarker-defined staging. Additionally, major observational cohorts (ADNI, BioFINDER) have repeatedly validated the high concordance of blood-based markers like p-tau217 with PET and autopsy standards. However, the document's criteria reflect a strong industry-driven push to streamline diagnosis and widen the addressable market for these therapies, moving faster than current FDA clearances for standalone blood diagnostics.
discrepancies: The document endorses highly accurate blood-based biomarkers (e.g., p-tau217) as standalone diagnostic tests for AD, but no standalone plasma assay has received full FDA clearance for this purpose yet (they currently act primarily as LDTs or triaging tools).

The criteria push a purely biological definition and staging of AD that includes asymptomatic individuals, but current FDA labels for approved anti-amyloid therapies strictly limit their use to patients actively exhibiting clinical symptoms (MCI or mild dementia).
